q: In the final accounts of a business, rent paid in advance (prepaid rent) is shown in the balance sheet as:
e: Prepaid rent is a payment for a benefit still to be received, so it is shown as a current asset.

q: A trader's capital at the beginning of the year was ₹2,00,000 and at the end of the year ₹2,80,000. During the year he introduced additional capital of ₹50,000 and withdrew ₹30,000 for personal use. What is his profit for the year?
e: Profit = closing capital − opening capital − additional capital + drawings = 2,80,000 − 2,00,000 − 50,000 + 30,000 = ₹60,000.

q: Which layer of the OSI reference model is responsible for data translation, encryption and compression?
e: The Presentation layer (layer 6) handles data format translation, encryption and compression.

q: What is the decimal equivalent of the hexadecimal number 2F?
What is the sum to infinity of the geometric series 6 + 3 + 1.5 + 0.75 + …?
What is the modulus of the complex number z = 5 − 12i?
What is the SI unit of magnetic flux density (magnetic field B)?
e: Magnetic flux density is measured in tesla (T), equal to one weber per square metre.

q: What is the power of a convex lens of focal length 25 cm?
Which of the following is a colligative property of a dilute solution?
e: Osmotic pressure depends only on the number of solute particles, so it is a colligative property.

q: 4 g of sodium hydroxide (molar mass 40 g/mol) is dissolved in water to make 500 mL of solution. What is the molarity of the solution?
e: Moles = 4/40 = 0.1 mol; molarity = 0.1 mol ÷ 0.5 L = 0.2 M.

q: Which enzyme synthesises the short RNA primers needed to start DNA synthesis during replication?
e: Primase (an RNA polymerase) lays down the RNA primers from which DNA polymerase extends the new strand.

q: Which plant tissue conducts water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the leaves?
e: Xylem conducts water and minerals upward from the roots; phloem transports food.

q: A curve showing all combinations of two goods that give a consumer the same level of satisfaction is called:
e: An indifference curve joins combinations of two goods that yield equal satisfaction to the consumer.

q: The total cost of producing 10 units of a good is ₹500 and the total cost of producing 11 units is ₹540. What is the marginal cost of the 11th unit?
Which function of management is concerned with recruiting, selecting, training and placing people in the positions of the organisation structure?
e: Staffing is the management function of filling and keeping filled the positions in the organisation.

q: Fayol's principle of 'unity of command' states that:
o: All activities with the same objective should have one head and one plan
Authority should flow from the top to the bottom in a chain
Individual interests should be subordinated to general interest
An employee should receive orders from one superior only
e: Unity of command means each employee should receive orders from, and be accountable to, only one superior (unity of direction is 'one head, one plan').

q: Who wrote 'Two Treatises of Government' (1689), which argued for natural rights to life, liberty and property?
e: John Locke wrote 'Two Treatises of Government', setting out the natural rights to life, liberty and property.

q: In a four-stroke internal combustion engine, one complete working cycle is completed in how many revolutions of the crankshaft?
e: A four-stroke engine completes its cycle (suction, compression, power, exhaust) in two revolutions of the crankshaft.
